pattern_name: Exact Frequency Map vs Count-Min Sketch
variant_desc: Chained hash-map<int,int> over 1M (key,inc) pairs (variable memory, hash-walk per insert) -> 2048x5 Count-Min Sketch (40 KB fixed, 5 cell updates per insert, min over 5 cells per query) (variant 3: seed=45, n_scale=2.0x)
source_citation: Cormode & Muthukrishnan, 'An Improved Data Stream Summary: The Count-Min Sketch and its Applications' (J. Alg 2005). arXiv:cs/0312050
novelty_rationale: Tests algorithmic recognition that exact frequency tracking can be replaced by a Count-Min Sketch when the user only needs upper-bound estimates for the hot keys (a top-K heavy-hitters workload). CMS is a one-sided estimator (always >= true count) with bounded eps*N additive error; choosing w/d trades memory for accuracy. No compiler converts a hash-map<int,int> into a 2D CMS array because the swap changes observable output (exact -> approximate); requires the model to reason about acceptable overestimation rather than per-loop micro-optimization.
